alerts.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 3 at 1:28AM EST until November 5 at 2:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.areas: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, and Coastal
Brevard Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Rough breaking surf of 4 to 6 feet
expected.

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 9:15PM EST until November 3 at 9:30AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.areas: Brevard, FL; Indian River, FL; Martin, FL; St. Lucie, FL
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida...
Eastern Indian River County in east central Florida...
Northeastern Martin County in east central Florida...
St. Lucie County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 930 AM EST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. It will take
several hours for all the water from the heavy rain that has
already fallen to work through local drainage systems in urban
areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 914 PM EST, Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated additional
downpours developing and moving over already saturated ground.
- This replaces the existing Flood Warning. If heavy rain persists,
additional Flash Flood Warnings may be required overnight.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Port Saint Lucie, Palm Bay, Melbourne, Walton, Fort Pierce,
Sebastian, Stuart, Vero Beach, Satellite Beach, Fellsmere, Indian
River Shores, Malabar, Indialantic, Vero Beach South, Gifford,
Winter Beach, Wabasso, Sebast

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 8:38PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused the St. Johns River near Cocoa to rise
into Minor Flood Stage. The river is forecast to rise through Minor
flood stage and into Moderate flood stage mid to late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 16.7 feet, Water covers yards, encroaches on homes and
may enter low lying homes along the St Johns River in the Lake
Poinsett area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM EST Monday the stage was 16.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 PM EST Monday was 16.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 16.8 feet Thursday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued November 2 at 1:37PM EST until November 3 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.areas: Inland Volusia; Okeechobee; Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Inland Northern Brevard; Inland Indian River; Inland St. Lucie; Inland Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Inland Southern Brevard; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of east central Florida, including the following
areas, Indian River, Martin, Saint Lucie, Volusia, Okeechobee and
Brevard.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy to extreme rainfall has occurred over coastal portions of
east central Florida today. Any additional rainfall overnight may
exacerbate ongoing flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

advisories.agency: Brevard County Sheriff's Office
advisories.text: Stay home and off the roadways unless necessary to travel to and from work or to escape high flooding. US 192 in Melbourne has flooded out. Expect significant delays.

advisories.agency: West Melbourne Police
advisories.text: Stay off the roads. Roads are flooded and cars are disabled throughout the city. Call 911 for life-or-death emergencies only.

advisories.agency: City of Palm Bay
advisories.text: Palm Bay City Hall and city offices closed today due to flooding. Widespread flooding in Palm Bay; avoid flooded roadways. Recreation facilities closed; trash collection cancelled today.

advisories.agency: Cocoa Beach Police
advisories.text: Never drive through standing water; stay indoors during the warning. No specific Cocoa Beach road closures posted.

advisories.agency: Brevard County Emergency Management
advisories.text: Limit water use: rain plus normal use is stressing the wastewater system (Cocoa Beach lift stations at capacity).

advisories.agency: Brevard Public Schools
advisories.text: All schools closed today due to flooding.

advisories.agency: Space Launch Delta 45 (Patrick SFB / Cape Canaveral SFS)
advisories.text: Non-mission-essential personnel should not report today because of hazardous roads and local flooding on base.

advisories.agency: City of Titusville
advisories.text: Wastewater system at capacity after overnight rain; controlled release of treated reclaimed water into the Indian River Lagoon began about 6:30 a.m. at the Osprey facility. Residents asked to cut nonessential water use (laundry, dishwashers, long showers) until further notice. Some Titusville streets impassable.

advisories.agency: Space Coast Area Transit (via WFTV)
advisories.text: Routes 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 27, 28 and 30 (Melbourne and Palm Bay area) suspended for Monday because of flooding. Routes 26 and 29 running with long delays; long delays on all other routes.

advisories.agency: Brevard County Government (via Spectrum News 13)
advisories.text: Brevard County government facilities closed countywide today because of flooding; all courts also closed.

advisories.agency: City of Palm Bay (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
advisories.text: Water shut off to several neighborhoods near Malabar Rd and Port Malabar Blvd after a water main break on Port Malabar Blvd NE; flooding prevents repairs. Boil water notice will apply once service is restored.

advisories.agency: City of Palm Bay Mayor (via News 6)
advisories.text: Fairhaven area of Palm Bay is inaccessible because of flooding; no specific roads named.

advisories.agency: City of Palm Bay (via Spectrum News 13)
advisories.text: Palm Bay officials declared a shelter-in-place on Monday morning because heavy rain is flooding streets and roads. Residents are asked to stay home and conserve water. Parts of Port Malabar Rd are washed out after Turkey Creek overflowed.

advisories.agency: City of Cocoa Beach (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
advisories.text: Waste Management warns that trash and recycling pickup in Cocoa Beach may be delayed because of heavy rain and flooding across Brevard County. City recreation facilities are closed.

advisories.agency: City of Melbourne (via The Weather Channel)
advisories.text: Melbourne City Hall is closed to the public because of flooding.

advisories.agency: City of Melbourne
advisories.text: Stay off the roads and shelter in place. Multiple roads closed by flooding, including Dubber Rd, North Dr, Stewart Rd, Dairy Rd at Edgewood Dr, and Edgewood Rd at Ruffner Rd. Avoid affected areas.

advisories.agency: State of Florida, Governor's Office (via WFTV)
advisories.text: State of emergency declared for Brevard and six other counties (Executive Order 26-227) because of flooding. Effective immediately for 60 days; includes price-gouging protections.

advisories.agency: Brevard Public Schools (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
advisories.text: Because of the extent of flooding across the county, all Brevard Public Schools campuses and district offices will stay closed Tuesday, Nov. 3. Schools are expected to reopen Wednesday.

advisories.agency: Brevard County Supervisor of Elections (via News 6)
advisories.text: Because of the historic flooding, some Election Day precinct polling locations are being moved temporarily for Tuesday's General Election. Voters should check where their precinct will vote before going.

advisories.agency: Brevard County Emergency Management (via Spectrum News 13)
advisories.text: Water on some roads has gone down since earlier in the day, but county officials still ask residents not to leave home unless they absolutely must or are under evacuation orders. The Red Cross has opened a shelter in Cocoa at Parker Memorial Missionary Baptist Church.

advisories.agency: Brevard County Supervisor of Elections (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
advisories.text: Because of flooding, the Supervisor of Elections offices in Titusville, Melbourne and Palm Bay are closed to the public until further notice. The Viera office at 2725 Judge Fran Jamieson Way is open, and its secure ballot intake station is taking completed mail ballots.

advisories.agency: Brevard County Sheriff's Office (via Space Coast Daily)
advisories.text: Sheriff Wayne Ivey says courts will be back in session Tuesday, Nov. 3, and many government offices are expected to reopen as flooding damage is assessed. Brevard Public Schools stay closed Tuesday so the district can inspect buildings. The full extent of flood damage is not yet known, so residents should stay off the roads unless they need to travel.
